method: Hand-written single-best-answer MCQs grounded only in the accepted open full text.

topic.coverageNote: Diagnosis, spur interpretation, and examination are grounded. A specific first-line injection protocol was not quoted because a clear 'first-line' sentence was not used.

mcqs.question: Which clinical pattern does the review describe for plantar fasciitis?

options.A: Pain with the first steps out of bed, often easing after activity starts, and tenderness at the medial calcaneal tubercle
options.B: Night pain only, with a warm swollen ankle
options.D: Pain exclusively on the dorsum of the midfoot

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Pain with the first steps out of bed, often easing after activity starts, and tenderness at the medial calcaneal tubercle
mcqs.explanation: Pain is worst with the first morning steps, may ease as activity begins and worsen later in the day, and tenderness may be at the medial calcaneal tubercle.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Pain often decreases after activities begin, but can worsen at the end of the day. Tenderness may present at the medial calcaneal tubercle.

mcqs.question: What performance does the review give for the windlass test?

options.D: Neither sensitivity nor specificity has been estimated
options.E: It is obsolete and should not be used

mcqs.explanation: The windlass test has high specificity (100%) but low sensitivity (32%), so it helps confirm the diagnosis more than it excludes it.

sourceRefs.excerpt: The windlass test [ Figure 1 ] have high specificity (100%) but low sensitivity (32%) for PF, which may be helpful in confirming the disease during physical examination.

mcqs.question: How should a calcaneal spur on a lateral radiograph be interpreted?

options.A: It is more common in plantar fasciitis than in controls in the cited study, but it can remain after symptoms resolve, so causation is not settled
options.B: The spur must be removed or pain cannot improve
options.D: Spurs occur only in people without heel pain

mcqs.correctAnswerText: It is more common in plantar fasciitis than in controls in the cited study, but it can remain after symptoms resolve, so causation is not settled
mcqs.explanation: One study found spurs in 89% of plantar fasciitis versus 32% of controls, but the review says causation needs further study and the spur remains after symptoms resolve.

sourceRefs.excerpt: the prevalence is significantly higher compared with the control group (89% vs. 32%), but the causal relationship needed to be further examined.

mcqs.question: What ultrasound findings does the review call major?

options.A: Increased plantar-fascia thickness and a hypoechoic plantar fascia
options.B: A Doppler-positive Morton neuroma as the required finding
options.C: A tear of the Achilles tendon in every case
options.D: Normal thickness excludes the need for any clinical exam
options.E: Ultrasound cannot assess the plantar fascia

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Increased plantar-fascia thickness and a hypoechoic plantar fascia
mcqs.explanation: Major sonographic findings are increased plantar-fascia thickness and a hypoechoic plantar fascia.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Major sonographic findings included increased plantar fascia thickness and hypoechoic plantar fascia

mcqs.question: How often is plantar fasciitis bilateral in this review?

options.A: Most cases are unilateral, but up to 30% are bilateral
options.D: Bilateral disease is limited to children

mcqs.correctAnswerText: Most cases are unilateral, but up to 30% are bilateral
mcqs.explanation: Most patients have unilateral disease, but up to 30% of cases are bilateral.

sourceRefs.excerpt: Most patients with PF are unilateral, but up to 30% of cases have a bilateral presentation.
